compatibility.title: Which Bentley Models Use the M177S?
compatibility.intro: The M177S is the 4.0-litre twin-turbo V8 found exclusively in the Bentley Bentayga S, unveiled in May 2021 as the most sporting member of the Bentayga family. It shares the same engine architecture as the standard Bentayga V8 (also 542 bhp / 770 Nm) but benefits from unique sports suspension calibration, Bentley Dynamic Ride active anti-roll control, and a more dynamic SPORT mode ESC tune.

failures.title: Bentley M177S Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: High-Pressure Fuel Pump Bolt Recall - Fire Risk
items.whatHappens: Bentley has issued recalls for certain V8 models (including the 4.0-litre KoVoMo Evo engine family) due to supplier improperly torquing the four screws that secure the high-pressure fuel pumps. This can lead to fuel leaks and, in extreme cases, a fire risk. This affects the M177S engine family.
items.repairVsReplace: This is a recall issue, not an engine-replacement problem. Affected vehicles should be taken to a Bentley dealer for inspection and correction. However, if a fuel leak has caused engine damage, a full rebuild or replacement may be required.

items.title: Turbocharger Oil Supply Screen Blockage
items.whatHappens: The Audi 4.0T (and Bentley 4.0T) V8 engines have been known to suffer from clogged turbo oil supply screens, which can starve the turbos of oil and lead to catastrophic turbo failure. On some cars, the cascading turbo failure damaged the engine and required a full replacement.
items.repairVsReplace: If caught early, the oil screen can be cleaned or replaced and the turbos inspected. If the turbos have failed and sent debris through the engine, a full replacement is often required.

items.title: Oil Leaks - Gaskets and Seals
items.whatHappens: Like many high-performance V8s, the M177S can develop oil leaks from gaskets, oil pan seals, and turbo oil feed lines. These are often caused by heat cycling and the stresses of high-performance driving.
items.repairVsReplace: Gasket and seal replacement is labour-intensive but not engine-replacement territory. Ignoring oil leaks that lead to low oil pressure can destroy the engine.

items.title: Ignition Coil Wear - Misfires and Rough Running
items.whatHappens: Bentley V8 engines can suffer from ignition coil failures, leading to misfires, hesitation under load, rough running, and increased fuel consumption.
items.repairVsReplace: Coil replacement is straightforward and not an engine-replacement issue. However, if misfires are ignored, they can lead to catalytic converter damage.

failures.goodYearsLine: The M177S is a relatively new engine (2021-present), and long-term reliability data is still emerging. The engine is part of the proven EA825 4.0-litre V8 family, which has a strong reputation when properly maintained. The high-pressure fuel pump bolt recall should be checked on all affected vehicles.

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the M177S
variants.intro: The M177S is the 4.0-litre twin-turbo V8 used in the Bentley Bentayga S. It produces 542 bhp (550 PS) and 568 lb.ft (770 Nm) of torque. The engine is part of the Volkswagen Group's EA825 4.0-litre V8 family, which also powers the Audi RS6, RS7, RS Q8, Porsche Panamera Turbo, and Lamborghini Urus. The engine code is stamped on the engine block - typically on a machined pad near the front or side of the engine. It also appears on the V5C registration document and can be retrieved via Bentley's VIN decoder. Key variants: - M177S (Bentayga S, 2021-present): 542 bhp (550 PS), 770 Nm. Unique sports suspension calibration, Bentley Dynamic Ride active anti-roll control, and Sport mode ESC tune. - 4.0 V8 (Bentayga V8, standard): Same power output (542 bhp, 770 Nm) but without the S-specific chassis and suspension enhancements. - 4.0 V8 (Continental GT V8 / Flying Spur V8): Different tuning, outputs vary by application. Not the M177S variant. - 4.0 V8 (Porsche / Audi applications): Different ECU calibrations, turbocharger specifications and ancillaries. Why fitting the wrong variant matters: The M177S has Bentley-specific tuning, ECU calibration and ancillaries. An Audi RS6 4.0-litre V8 or Porsche Panamera Turbo engine is not a direct swap for the Bentayga S unit - engine mounts, wiring looms, cooling systems and transmission compatibility all differ.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement M177S - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used M177S can make sense for lower‑value Bentayga S examples where a £14,000+ reconditioned engine would approach the car's value. But with used units, service history and recall status are everything - an M177S with an outstanding high‑pressure fuel pump bolt recall or a history of oil starvation is a major gamble. Only buy a used unit with documented full service history and confirmation that any recalls have been addressed. View used engines

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper M177S recon addresses the high‑pressure fuel pump bolts (per the recall), replaces all gaskets and seals, inspects and cleans the turbo oil supply screens, inspects and refurbishes the twin turbochargers, and performs a full carbon clean. This is the right call for any Bentayga S worth more than £50,000-£60,000, or where you plan to keep the car long‑term. The 12-24 month warranty is essential given the complexity. View reconditioned engines

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified for high‑value Bentayga S examples or where the original engine has matching‑numbers value. An upgraded rebuild should include new timing chain components, upgraded turbocharger cores, forged pistons and a full bottom‑end refresh. The M177S is not a DIY proposition - only a specialist with Bentley V8 experience should undertake this work. View rebuilt engines

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: All our vetted UK Bentley specialists can supply and fit your M177S - nationwide delivery, 12‑month warranty on reconditioned and rebuilt units, and fitting typically completed within 2-4 weeks. View supply and fit VEHICLE VALUE NOTE (mandatory): The M177S typically sits in vehicles worth £80,000-£180,000+. With a reconditioned unit at £14,000-£24,000+ plus fitting, the total cost can reach £17,000-£28,000+. For a Bentayga S, this represents approximately 15-30% of the vehicle's value - generally a justifiable expense for a high‑value luxury SUV. However, always evaluate the specific vehicle's condition and market value before committing. Always get a professional inspection before committing to any replacement.

items.question: What are the most common problems with the Bentley M177S engine?
items.answer: The most common issues are related to the high‑pressure fuel pump bolt recall (a fire risk if not addressed), turbocharger oil supply screen blockage (which can starve the turbos), and oil leaks from gaskets and seals. Ignition coil wear causing misfires is also reported. The high‑pressure fuel pump bolt recall should be checked on all affected vehicles, clogged oil screens can lead to catastrophic turbo failure, and regular maintenance prevents most major issues.

items.question: Should I buy a used, reconditioned or rebuilt M177S?
items.answer: Used M177S units (£8,000-£15,000) can work for lower‑value Bentayga S examples, but only with full service history and confirmation that the fuel pump recall has been addressed. Reconditioned units (£14,000-£24,000+) are the best bet for most owners - they address the fuel pump bolts, oil screens, turbos and all gaskets. Rebuilt units (£18,000-£30,000+) are for high‑value Bentayga S models where matching numbers or a full refresh is justified. Always prioritise a unit with the fuel pump recall completed, a 12-24 month warranty is essential given the complexity, and factor in fitting costs (£2,500-£4,800) when comparing.

items.question: How do I tell if my car has the M177S and not another Bentley V8?
items.answer: The engine code is stamped on a machined pad on the block, typically near the front or side. It also appears on your V5C and can be retrieved via Bentley's VIN decoder. The M177S is unique to the Bentayga S - if your car is a Bentayga S, it has the M177S. The standard Bentayga V8 uses the same engine architecture but with different chassis tuning, the Continental GT V8 and Flying Spur V8 are different variants, and check your V5C or Bentley VIN decoder for the exact engine code.

items.question: How reliable is the Bentley M177S engine compared to other Bentayga engines?
items.answer: The M177S is part of the proven EA825 4.0‑litre V8 family, which has a strong reputation when properly maintained. The fuel pump bolt recall is the only significant known issue - once addressed, the engine is considered robust. It offers the same power as the standard Bentayga V8 but with sportier chassis tuning. Regular oil changes (every 6,000-8,000 miles) are critical, the turbo oil supply screens should be inspected at major service intervals, and the M177S benefits from the proven EA825 architecture.
